group.passage: On a cold morning, you can pour hot soup into a vacuum flask and still enjoy it warm at lunch. On a summer day, the same bottle keeps ice water cold for hours. Few people know that this everyday object began as a tool for scientists who studied extreme cold. Its inventor, James Dewar, grew up in Scotland and later worked in London, where he became director of the Royal Institution in 1887. Dewar studied gases that had been cooled until they turned into liquids. Such liquids are far colder than ice, so in an ordinary container they warm up and boil away very quickly. To slow this down, Dewar placed one glass bottle inside another, pumped the air out of the space between them, and coated the glass with silver. Each part of the design blocks a different path for heat. Because the two walls do not touch, heat cannot easily pass from one wall to the other. With no air in the gap, nothing can carry heat across it. The shiny silver works like a mirror and sends heat rays back where they came from. Since heat has trouble getting in or out, cold things stay cold and hot things stay hot. In December 1892, Dewar showed his flask at an evening lecture. He wanted to prove that the empty space did the heavy lifting, so he broke the tip of a flask that held liquid oxygen. As soon as air rushed into the gap, the oxygen began to boil wildly. Dewar made his flask for science, but others saw a chance to sell it. In 1904, a German company called Thermos began selling vacuum bottles for use at home. By 1907, companies in the United States, Canada, and Britain had bought the rights to the Thermos name. In 1911, a British company made the first glass inner bottle by machine. By 2004, four out of five Americans owned one.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: Why liquid oxygen boils so wildly when air reaches it.
options.B: How British companies competed to build better tools for science.
options.C: How a lab tool for very cold liquids found its way into homes.
options.D: Why three countries fought each other over the right to use the Thermos name.

options.B: He wanted to keep his soup hot until lunch.
options.C: His glass bottles kept breaking during his lectures.
options.D: The Royal Institution asked him to design a bottle it could sell.

options.B: Made the flask too heavy to hold.
options.C: Let air flow into the gap.
options.D: Did most of the important work.

options.B: Companies in three countries gained the right to the Thermos name.

1.explanation_zh: 第一段就說，這個日常用品原本是研究極低溫的科學家使用的工具；第二到四段介紹杜瓦為了保存極冷的液體做出雙層真空瓶、它怎麼擋住熱，以及他在演講中的示範；最後一段說別人看到商機，保溫瓶進入一般家庭。全文講的是實驗室的低溫工具如何變成家用保溫瓶。
evidence: Few people know that this everyday object began as a tool for scientists who studied extreme cold.
Dewar made his flask for science, but others saw a chance to sell it.

option_notes_zh.A: 液態氧在空氣進入夾層後劇烈沸騰，只是第四段示範的一個細節（文中確實有 the oxygen began to boil wildly），不是全文主旨。
option_notes_zh.B: 文中只說一家英國公司在 1911 年用機器做出玻璃內膽，沒有談英國公司互相競爭製造科學工具。
option_notes_zh.D: 文中說美國、加拿大和英國的公司「買下」Thermos 名稱的權利，沒有說三個國家為此爭吵。

To slow this down, Dewar placed one glass bottle inside another, pumped the air out of the space between them, and coated the glass with silver.

option_notes_zh.C: 文中說的是杜瓦在演講中「故意」敲斷一個瓶子的尖端來示範，不是瓶子在演講時一直破掉。
option_notes_zh.D: 杜瓦是皇家研究院的院長；文中說的是後來「別人」看到商機才開始販賣，研究院沒有要他設計瓶子來賣。

2.strategy_zh: 找杜瓦「研究什麼」以及「To slow this down」前面的那個問題：極冷的液體在普通容器裡很快就沸騰消失。

evidence: He wanted to prove that the empty space did the heavy lifting, so he broke the tip of a flask that held liquid oxygen.

option_notes_zh.A: 只看字面「舉起重物」才會選；文中的主詞是 the empty space（真空夾層），它不會搬瓶子。
option_notes_zh.B: 文中完全沒有說瓶子太重；只看到 heavy 這個字的字面意思。

3.strategy_zh: 片語的主詞是 the empty space；再看下一句：空氣一進入，液態氧就沸騰。表示真空夾層是保冷的關鍵。

translation_zh.text:
在寒冷的早晨，你可以把熱湯倒進保溫瓶，到了午餐時間還能喝到溫熱的湯。在夏天，同一個瓶子能讓冰水冷上好幾個小時。很少人知道，這個日常用品一開始是研究極低溫的科學家所使用的工具。
它的發明者詹姆斯‧杜瓦在蘇格蘭長大，後來在倫敦工作，並在 1887 年成為英國皇家研究院的院長。杜瓦研究被冷卻到變成液體的氣體。這種液體比冰冷得多，所以放在普通容器裡，很快就會變暖並沸騰消失。為了減緩這種情形，杜瓦把一個玻璃瓶放進另一個玻璃瓶裡，把兩者之間的空氣抽掉，並在玻璃上鍍了一層銀。
這個設計的每個部分都擋住熱的一條路徑。因為兩層瓶壁互不接觸，熱很難從一層傳到另一層。夾層裡沒有空氣，就沒有東西能把熱帶過去。亮晶晶的銀像鏡子一樣，把熱輻射反射回原處。熱很難進出，所以冷的東西保持冷，熱的東西保持熱。
1892 年 12 月，杜瓦在一場晚間演講中展示了他的瓶子。他想證明真空的夾層才是功臣，於是敲斷一個裝著液態氧的瓶子尖端。空氣一衝進夾層，液態氧就開始劇烈沸騰。
杜瓦做這個瓶子是為了科學，但別人看見了販賣的機會。1904 年，一家名叫 Thermos 的德國公司開始販售家用的保溫瓶。到了 1907 年，美國、加拿大和英國的公司已經買下 Thermos 這個名稱的權利。1911 年，一家英國公司首次用機器製造玻璃內膽。到了 2004 年，每五個美國人就有四個擁有保溫瓶。
